p: The clue's in the address: this Flip Out sits on the retail and business park beside Aintree Racecourse, the home of the Grand National. Every spring, the Grand National Festival brings huge crowds to the area, so if your visit lands during the meeting in April, expect very busy roads and plan your journey accordingly.

If you'd rather leave the car behind, Aintree station is on the Merseyrail Northern line, with trains running through from Liverpool city centre. It's a simple trip, and it saves the bother of parking at busy times.

North Liverpool has some brilliant places to pair with a session. Croxteth Hall and Country Park has a historic hall, a working farm with animals, a walled garden and wide parkland to explore. It's a lovely contrast to the noise of a trampoline arena.

Head towards the coast, and Crosby Beach is home to Another Place, Antony Gormley's famous installation of a hundred cast-iron figures staring out to sea. Seeing them appear and disappear with the tide is a little bit magical, and it's free.
A bit further up the coast, Formby is famous for its red squirrels and sand dunes, managed by the National Trust, and it's a fantastic place for a run-around and a nature spot.
Football fans will also know that Anfield, home of Liverpool FC, is only a few miles away, and the stadium tour is a big draw for young supporters.
With so much on the doorstep, an hour or two of bouncing could easily become the start of a much bigger day out.
